ctx.x: And of course, there were a certain number of people who snuck off to the Red Light District to listen to piano players. And they would relate this to me. They didn't seem particularly ashamed of it, and sang it even in mixed company then.

Of course, you also got people with some other attitudes. I remember, you remember this book of, this book of Belok's pictures that, that Lee Friedlander did with the... items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-07-31
items.q: when I met Johnny Wiggs and liked him... they had been in high school together and apparently had been good friends... I don't think Johnny ever told me about that.

ctx.x: You still haven't talked about the thing originally entitled the Hiawatha, the Indian and a Mezzo. Do you know what that is? No. That's the original name of the The Lizard on the Rail. Oh really? Yeah, and Tony Perrini recorded it. I thought I would have played that for

it. No. I think I did hear the Perrini record. And Johnny used to play it, Johnny Wiggs. Yeah, well my mother used to, and I don't quite know where she picked it up from, but she used to sometimes sing a very brief business about there's a lizard on the rail, on the rail, on the rail, with his tail coupe. And is that how it goes in the...
Well I think Johnny sang it as, with his tail cut off, but exactly the same. Hmm. Johnny Wiggs. No, I'd forgotten that. Wiggs. Which is another old circuit.
